p01.why: With spaces, 0xe and 1 are separate literals giving 15, and 1e+1 is a floating literal of value 10.

p02.why: 1u8 is one literal with the suffix u8, which is not a valid integer suffix and names no literal operator.

p03.why: 1e999f is outside the range of float: Clang and GCC accept it with a warning and give infinity, EDG rejects it (Q-0063).

p04.why: uz gives std::size_t, z gives the matching signed type, so 1z - 2z is negative.

p05.why: With -m32 the ordinary encoding is UTF-8 and the wide encoding UTF-32, so every assertion holds on Clang and GCC; EDG skips -m32 tests.

p06.why: The f32 and F64 suffixes are conditionally supported: GCC and EDG accept them, Clang rejects them.

p07.why: A hexadecimal floating literal must have a binary exponent.

p08.why: A string literal is an lvalue of an array of N const characters, with N counting the null, so decltype gives a reference to that array.

p09.why: v finds n::v (2) and ::v finds the global v (1), giving 21.

p10.why: this cannot be used in a static member function.

p11.why: 0xe+1 without spaces is one numeric run, which is not a valid literal.

p12.why: Clang and GCC use UTF-8 and UTF-32 and accept every assertion; EDG, as configured, rejects the string "é".

p14.why: U+1F600 needs two UTF-16 code units, so it does not fit in one char16_t.

p15.why: A u-prefixed character literal must hold one character.

p16.why: nullptr converts to every pointer-to-member type.

p17.why: this cannot be used outside a class.

p18.why: A fold expression must be in parentheses.

p19.why: 0.1 rounds to the nearer double, which is exactly 3602879701896397 / 2^55, and the float value differs from the double value.

p21.why: A parenthesized function name is still the function, so the call returns 3.

p22.why: The operand 2 * V holds a binary operator without parentheses: Clang and GCC reject, EDG accepts (Q-0194).

p24.why: Unsuffixed floating literals are double, f gives float, and L gives long double.

p25.why: A raw string keeps each character, so the sizes count the backslash and the inner quote and parenthesis.

p26.why: Adjacent string literals with two different prefixes cannot be joined.

p27.why: A fold over + with no extra operand needs at least one element.

p28.why: A decimal literal takes the first of int, long, long long that holds it, and long is 64 bits on the target.

p29.why: Each simple escape gives the code unit of its character in every prefix.

p30.why: 1.2.3 is one numeric run that is not a valid literal.

p32.why: \x41 ends at the backslash, so the string holds a, A, new-line, and the null.

p33.why: The hexadecimal escape 0x100 is too large for char.

p34.why: this can be used in a default member initializer and points to s.

p35.why: The decimal literal fits only an unsigned type: Clang and GCC reject under -pedantic-errors, EDG accepts (Q-0064).

p36.why: A function name is an lvalue, so a reference binds to it and & takes its address.

p37.why: A character literal must contain at least one character.

p38.why: Clang and GCC warn about the out-of-range literal and -Werror makes the warning an error; EDG skips -Werror tests.

p39.why: A string literal does not convert to a pointer to non-const char.

p41.why: this has the cv-qualifiers of the member function.

p42.why: A raw string delimiter must not contain a space.

p43.why: this cannot be used in a function with an explicit object parameter.

p44.why: v and this->v both name the member, so get returns 6.

p45.why: A string literal is an array lvalue, so its address has type pointer to const char[4], and it converts to const char*.

p46.why: The base prefix 0b has no digit after it.

p47.why: The octal escape 0777 (511) is too large for char.

p48.why: A universal character name must not name a surrogate.

p49.why: Whether the two literals share an object is unspecified, but the condition is true either way.

p50.why: f names the function and returns 2.

p51.why: N is not a pack, so no operand names an unexpanded pack.

p52.why: nullptr does not convert to an integer.

p53.why: A string literal is an array, so it can be subscripted and dereferenced in a constant expression.

p54.why: In a const member function, v is a const lvalue and cannot be assigned.

p55.why: The digits have consecutive code units in every encoding.

p56.why: S::count names the static member (3) and S::size the enumerator (4).

p57.why: An enumerator is a prvalue, and & needs an lvalue.

p58.why: Clang and GCC warn about a multi-character literal, and -Werror makes the warning an error; EDG skips -Werror tests.

p59.why: A universal character name can name a basic character, so \u0041 is A.

p60.why: S::v names a non-static member outside a member function in an evaluated operand.

p61.why: true is bool, nullptr converts to object and function pointers and to bool by direct initialization.

p62.why: The base prefix 0x has no digit after it.

p63.why: Both operands name an unexpanded pack.

p64.why: Plain char is signed on the x86-64 Linux targets.

p65.why: this is a prvalue, so its address cannot be taken.

p66.why: Binary, octal, and hexadecimal prefixes and digit separators between digits give these values.

p67.why: Each one-character literal has its UTF-8, UTF-16, or UTF-32 code unit, and escapes give their number converted to the type; EDG's handling of non-ASCII source here is not stated.

p68.why: The suffixes pick the unsigned and long forms, and 4294967296u needs unsigned long.

p69.why: A raw string delimiter must not contain a parenthesis.

p70.why: The prefix sets the type of a character literal.

p71.why: 2_k uses a literal operator, and p takes a sign in a hexadecimal floating literal.

p72.why: Each literal spells the same value as its comparison, and the separator sits between digits.

p74.why: A universal character name can name a control character.

p76.why: A raw string delimiter must not contain a backslash.

p77.why: Adjacent literals join, and the prefix of one carries to the result.

p78.why: nullptr converts to bool only by direct initialization, and this is copy initialization.

p79.why: A floating literal must not have an integer suffix.

p80.why: A multi-character literal has type int, and 'ab' is 0x6162 on the targets.

p81.why: Writing to a string literal is undefined; the literal sits in read-only memory, so the write faults and ASan reports it.

p82.why: Unicode defines no character with that name.

p83.why: The comma fold runs in order, and the && and || folds stop at the second element as the written-out expressions do.

p84.why: 2147483648 is long, and the minus sign is a separate operator, so the type is long.

p85.why: é needs two UTF-8 code units, and no implementation in the matrix accepts such an unprefixed literal.

p86.why: u8 and u are different prefixes.

p87.why: this can be used in the trailing return type of a member function.

p88.why: A parenthesized lvalue stays an lvalue, so both assignments work.

p89.why: m is a member of O, but g runs on an I object, so there is no O object for m.

p90.why: lul is not one of the suffix forms.

p91.why: A variable name is an lvalue.

p92.why: Each escape form, including the braced \x{} and \o{} forms, gives the stated value.

p93.why: A mutable member can change in a const function, and the const pointer member still points to a non-const int.

p95.why: A 16-character delimiter is allowed, and the string holds x and the null.

p96.why: The last separator has no digit after it.

p97.why: In a const member function, v is const and cannot be assigned.

p98.why: The separator has the prefix x before it, and not a digit.

p99.why: The named escape gives the character with that Unicode name.

p100.why: Lookup finds no declaration of the name.

p101.why: A static member function has no object, so the non-static member v cannot be used there.

p102.why: Writing to a string literal during constant evaluation is undefined.

p103.why: A parenthesized literal is still a prvalue, so decltype gives the plain type.

p104.why: Comparing the addresses of two string literals during constant evaluation: Clang rejects, GCC and EDG accept (Q-0033).

p105.why: A raw string delimiter must not contain a tab.

p106.why: 2^64 does not fit in any type in the list.

p107.why: The delimiter has 17 characters, and the limit is 16.

p108.why: The two operators of a fold with an extra operand must be the same.

p109.why: é does not fit in one UTF-8 code unit.

p110.why: Each fold nests as stated, empty folds over &&, ||, comma, and with an extra operand are valid, and the .* fold reaches 7.

p111.why: Whether two evaluations give one object is unspecified, and the condition is true either way.

p112.why: Hexadecimal and octal literals take the unsigned form when the signed one cannot hold the value.

p113.why: The operand of sizeof is unevaluated, so a non-static member name is valid there.

p114.why: ull gives unsigned long long, which holds the value.
